title: update.py freezes worktree dispatchers more than one engine generation behind, silently stripping every new command
body:
`reconcile_linked_dispatchers` (.super-coder/scripts/update.py:809-886) lays the current dispatcher into linked worktrees, but only when the worktree's `sc` bytes match a recognized "managed" version. The managed set is built at lines 847-871 from exactly three sources: that worktree's own `HEAD:sc`, `sc` at `.sc-state/engine.ref`, and `sc` at `.sc-state/engine.ref.prev`. Anything else is declared a local edit and skipped with a warning (lines 872-877).

That window is two engine generations deep. A worktree dispatcher older than `engine.ref.prev` matches nothing in the set, is misclassified as hand-edited, and is left stale. The misclassification is self-perpetuating: because the file is never rewritten, every later update pushes `engine.ref`/`engine.ref.prev` further forward and the stale copy falls further outside the window. It can never be reconciled again by any number of `./sc update` runs.

Reproduced in the live downstream repo, /home/j3d1/Repos/rst-c, correctly reconciled to engine.ref `3780151ee2cb`:

- root `sc` is the current 55-line bootstrap (md5 7429accd6ab70e2bbf0bf8a5031f2b2e);
- `.sc-worktrees/{cart1,dev1,dev2,pln1}/sc` are all byte-identical to each other at 1736 lines (md5 797724b5022a8aec81cc5f3cc145712b), which equals neither their own `HEAD:sc` (md5 523c9957cbdd741ab044ffeceee2e0fa) nor `sc` at engine.ref or engine.ref.prev (003f6ae78d8a);
- only `.sc-worktrees/rev1/sc` matches and is current.

Four independent branches carrying one byte-identical file is not four hand edits. I traced the blob: `git hash-object` gives df744382e3c1df7e3e199346d773ecfad2ea4f48, which is exactly the tracked `sc` at rst-c commit 6a34bc12fc17b595f34b00f5fce80c0145fb1ee4, "chore(engine): repin to 3d1f9f3" (2026-08-02). It is engine-shipped content from an older generation, not user modification. The "local edits are preserved and named rather than overwritten" heuristic in the docstring is misfiring on the engine's own artifact.

Consequence: that 1736-line file predates the spec #105 single-owner-dispatcher migration. It is a self-contained dispatcher with its own command table and no `vm` case; its line 1735 is `*) echo "sc: unknown command '$cmd' (try ./sc help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;`. Any shell booted in one of those four worktrees silently runs an engine floor from before the migration and loses every command added since — the entire `vm` surface this Sprint delivered, and `sc sprint` besides. The failure is silent and misattributable: the operator sees a correctly reconciled root, a correct `engine.ref`, and a command that reports itself unknown.

This is what invalidated Sprint 2's downstream acceptance gate. Unit 17 launched its acceptance shell in rst-c's `dev1` worktree with `SC_HARNESS=codex` correctly set, and its first preflight command `./sc vm status --json` returned that exact error at exit 2, aborting the run before any VM contact.

Fix boundary: widen managed-version recognition past the two-ref window so an engine-shipped dispatcher of any age is recognized as managed — for example by testing the worktree's `sc` blob against `sc` at commits reachable along the engine line, or by keeping a content-hash record of shipped dispatcher versions. Do not narrow it to a forced overwrite: preserving genuine local edits is correct and should survive the fix. Out of spec #108's scope; belongs to the spec #105 dispatcher lane.

title: Spec #108 downstream acceptance gate is unproven after three attempts and did not converge
body:
Spec #108 line 182 requires that a live Codex launch show the Windows MCP tools on its first turn, and line 188 requires one `rst-c` session exercising push, complex exec, capture, `mcp up`, one GUI observation/action, and `mcp down`. Neither has ever been satisfied.

Three attempts, three distinct blockers, none anticipated by the previous one:

- Unit 12 (12:24) and unit 14 (13:29): `mcp up` returned structured `mcp_adapter_unsupported` / `SC_HARNESS is not set`. Both runs were performed by subfloor-launched shells that reached rst-c by `cd`, so `SC_HARNESS` was never exported. No GUI action possible or claimed.
- Unit 17 (14:21): the launch defect was corrected — rst-c reconciled and pinned to `3780151`, shell launched inside rst-c, `SC_HARNESS=codex` proven set — and the run still stopped at its first preflight command with `sc: unknown command 'vm'`, per finding 1.

The engine behaved correctly at every step, including refusing `up` before any transport mutation and aborting preflight rather than proceeding. Both Developers and the unit 17 runner correctly reported unconfirmed results and claimed no success, satisfying spec line 192. Unit 17 explicitly self-declared its report INVALID and not gate evidence.

What remains unknown is material: because unit 17 never got past preflight, the parts of the gate beyond `vm status` — managed MCP injection presenting Windows MCP tools on a first turn, `mcp up` reaching a verified endpoint, and any GUI observation/action — have still never been exercised end to end by any run. Clearing finding 1 is necessary but may not be sufficient; a fourth attempt could surface a fourth blocker.

Consequence: the Sprint's automated acceptance is fully met and green (1942 passed, 947 subtests, at `3780151`), but the live downstream behavior that motivated the Sprint is unverified. No fork should be told the Windows MCP GUI seam is proven downstream.

Fix boundary: not an in-Sprint patch. This needs a successor Sprint that owns finding 1's dispatcher fix first and then re-runs the gate from a worktree with a current dispatcher (or from the repo root), under a single authorized VM lane preserving the supplied-state / no-opening-reset / no-mid-session-reset / single-final-`reset --off` contract. Escalated to FnB as non-convergence rather than started as a third re-entry episode.

title: 21 liveness escalations fired across the Sprint, all first-episode, all self-resolved
body:
The anomaly stream records 21 `liveness.escalated` events between 07:04 and 14:04, every one at `silence_episode: 1` with `planner_delivery_route: delivery-time`. Wake health at close shows 129 delivered, 0 failed wakes, 0 nudges, and 0 open liveness expectations against 45 resolved. One `pr.poll_failed` at 09:03:51 (GitHub read unavailable on PR 1028) backed off 10s and recovered.

So nothing wedged and no delivery was lost. But 21 first-episode escalations across roughly seven hours of a Sprint that never paused is a high enough rate to be worth a look: either the silence threshold is tuned tighter than real reviewer and developer turn times, or escalation is firing on turns that are progressing normally. Recorded as an observation for FnB disposition, not a delivery defect.

Fix boundary: none proposed. If FnB wants this pursued, it is a measurement question first — compare the configured grace interval against observed turn durations in this Sprint's timeline before changing any threshold.
